⁣
This movie isn’t about aviation. That inverted sequence, as jaw-dropping as it is, is just the hook. A sucker punch to get your attention. The real story? Addiction. Denial. A man spiraling so far into his own lies that even his greatest act of heroism, saving nearly everyone on board, can’t erase the wreckage of his private life.⁣
⁣
Captain Whip Whitaker (Denzel Washington) is the kind of character you don’t want to look at too closely, because you might see parts of yourself reflected back. He’s brilliant, charismatic, utterly competent at his job… But a complete trainwreck everywhere else. He drinks like his liver signed a suicide pact. He snorts cocaine just to level out. He wakes up hungover and climbs into a cockpit as if that’s just another Tuesday. He’s the definition of functional disaster.⁣
⁣
Denzel owns this role. I mean owns it. He plays Whip with such raw precision that you find yourself hating him, loving him and pitying him. All in the same scene. He’s a hero, no doubt. He pulled off the impossible. But he’s also a liar and a danger to everyone around him. And here’s the kicker: you still root for him. You don’t want him to crash, figuratively or literally. That’s the magic trick Zemeckis pulls off. He makes you care about someone you should probably not care about.⁣
⁣
So yeah, Flight (2012) isn’t a movie about flying. It’s a movie about falling. About how far you can go before you finally admit you’ve hit the ground. It’s a story about addiction so accurate that treatment centers literally use it in group therapy. And it’s Denzel at his absolute best, in a performance so good it should be studied in acting schools. Forget the physics. Forget the inverted roll. The real miracle of Flight (2012) is that it takes a broken, lying, substance-soaked man and makes you care enough to hope he lands. ⁣

source_details.synopsis: Flight is a 2012 American drama film directed by Robert Zemeckis, written by John Gatins and produced by Walter F. Parkes, Laurie MacDonald, Steve Starkey, Zemeckis, and Jack Rapke. The film stars Denzel Washington as William "Whip" Whitaker Sr., an alcoholic airline pilot who miraculously crash-lands his plane after a mechanical failure, saving nearly everyone on board. Although hailed a hero, an investigation soon begins to cast the captain in a different light. Flight premiered at the New York Film Festival on October 14, 2012, and was theatrically released the following month on November 2, 2012 by Paramount Pictures. It received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised Washi
